requirement:
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.

When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
rationale:
**Judgment: the requirement is met.** Both obligations are implemented, the implementation is marked, and the tests cover the main design points.

## Implementation

**Initial mandatory set.**
- `AssessmentSources::prepare` (src/authoring/inputs.rs) builds the contributed selectors:
  - the subject itself;
  - `{cite}`d requirements;
  - `{impl}`/`{test}` source nodes;
  - `:impl:`/`:test:` anchors.
- It passes the resulting `mandatory` inputs and the subject text to `definition_inputs`.
- `definition_inputs` calls `terms::dependencies`, which gathers `{term}` references from:
  - the subject text;
  - Rust comments in contributed source nodes;
  - Markdown or plain text in other files;
  - bodies of requirement declarations.
- `terms::close_dependencies` expands them to a fixed point, using a `visited` set and a `BTreeSet`. That gives the transitive closure with no duplicates and guaranteed termination on cycles.
- Each resulting name goes through `source_input` as an `InputSelector::Definition`. Its text is the complete raw fenced declaration, including the `:phrase:` line.
- `prepare` appends these to `mandatory` only if not already present, so they are deduplicated.
- Unresolvable terms produce errors before inference.
- The built-in texts contain no `{term}` references, so omitting them from term scanning loses nothing.

**Additional reads.**
- `read` and `search` (src/authoring/tools.rs) call `AssessmentSources::additional_definitions` on the newly delivered inputs.
  - It returns the transitive definitions, filtered against the delivered inputs and `recorded`.
  - These are returned in the tool result, so they are supplied to the model, and also added to `ToolDelivery.inputs`.
- `converse` (src/authoring/mod.rs) pushes the delivered inputs to `pending`. It calls `record_inputs` after the next successful response, including the submission turn and before `parse`. So they are recorded before a submission is accepted.
- `record_inputs` deduplicates.

**Marking.** The implementing pieces are marked `{impl}` for this requirement: `prepare`, `record_inputs`, `additional_definitions`, `source_input`, `definition_inputs`, `converse`, `read` and `search`. The closure logic in `src/terms.rs` is marked with `requirements.definitions.dependencies` and `requirements.definitions.selection`. Their text covers the transitive, cycle-safe, deduplicated fixed point, which is exactly what this requirement relies on.

## Tests

- **`bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors`**
  - A term is referenced by the subject.
  - The term set is the transitive set `unit` and `value`, where `unit` references `value`.
  - Exactly 2 definition inputs are asserted, so there are no duplicates.
  - Earlier evidence inputs are not carried forward.
- **`mandatory_git_inputs_require_staging_declarations_sources_and_terms`**
  - A term referenced from a contributed source file becomes a mandatory definition input.
  - A term declaration file that is not staged produces an error.
- **`definitions_introduced_by_a_read_are_supplied_and_recorded_before_submission`**
  - The terms form a cycle (`value` and `unit` reference each other), so cycle termination is tested.
  - The read introduces the terms. The delivered set is `["terms.unit","terms.value"]`, once each.
  - Each definition's text starts with `:::{definition}` and `:phrase:`.
  - The terms are absent from the first request, present in the second request, and in the recorded evidence inputs. This shows they are delivered and recorded before the submission.
- **`reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms`** covers the `habeas` read path and repeated recording without duplicates.
- **`search_supplies_terminology_clamps_at_eof_and_reports_failures`** covers the `ripgrep` path.
- **`term_dependencies_of_every_markdown_extension_skip_literal_roles`** (src/terms.rs, marked for `requirements.definitions.dependencies`, not this requirement) covers the scanning rules.

Coverage spans direct, transitive, cyclic, duplicate, source-read, search and recording-before-submission cases. I found no unacknowledged gaps.

text: :::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
